The Nashville star spoke openly about her strained relationship with her mother, who was her manager during her rise to fame as a child star. The two were estranged at the time of Panettiere’s death, and the actor had told podcaster Jay Shetty in May that Vogel “didn’t care to have a relationship with me.”
Vogel served as Panettiere’s manager from the time she was just an infant.
The actor opened up about her relationship with her mother in an interview with The Independent in May.
“She’s a very complex person,” Panettiere said. “I don’t want to offend anybody, or drag anybody, or hurt anyone’s feelings. But I knew that if I wasn’t honest about my relationship with her, I wouldn’t be being honest at all. She’s a huge part of the person I am today.”
Panettiere cut professional ties with Vogel at the age of 19, while working on Heroes. In her memoir, released earlier this year, she said she asked Vogel to meet her in her trailer and begged her to just be her mother.
“All I wanted was a dynamic that didn’t involve contracts, producers, boho tops, or drinking wine at industry parties,” she wrote.
Vogel, Panettiere claimed, “picked up her purse, clenched her jaw, and looked straight at me. ‘You owe me,’ she answered. Then she turned around and walked out of my trailer ... I knew I’d done the right thing, but I sensed something in me had died.”
summary: Hayden Panettiere's estranged mother, Lesley Vogel, has strongly criticized CBS Mornings host Gayle King for lacking compassion and professionalism. King had publicly slammed Vogel's remarks regarding the death of her 36-year-old daughter, calling them an unfortunate final message from a mother. Vogel stated that King never reached out to her beforehand and called the attacks shameful.
key_points: Hayden Panettiere passed away at the age of 36 following a cardiac arrest in South Carolina.
Lesley Vogel criticized Gayle King's on-air remarks reacting to Vogel's initial statements about her daughter's death.
King had publicly condemned Vogel's comments on CBS Mornings, remarking, 'Thanks, Mom, for nothing.'
Panettiere and her mother had a historically complex and estranged relationship, with Vogel having served as her manager since infancy until Panettiere cut professional ties at age 19.

Olden — from Middle English olden, based on old + -en. Originally simply “old,” it survives mainly in the phrase “olden times,” meaning former or ancient times.
Be sure to follow me for all your daily puzzle-solving guides, TV show and movie reviews and more here on this blog!

title: Climber Laura completes 'full house' of 1,072 peaks around UK
author: Paul Hastie
content:
![Person taking a selfie on a rocky mountain ridge, wearing a red hiking top and backpack, with rugged stone formations, grassy slopes, and dramatic cloudy skies in the background.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/7c73/live/a8bb2dc0-9e44-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Laura has become part of the elite group to complete the "full house"
- Published
It is a big day for Scottish climber Laura Baillie who has completed the "full house" of the UK's highest peaks.
Reaching the top of Carn na h-Easgainn in the Highlands, the 38-year-old becomes one of an elite group of about 100 people who have stood on all 1,072 summits.
To complete the Scottish Mountaineering Club challenge, hikers must tick off every Munro, Munro Top, Corbett, Graham and Donald in Scotland - as well as every Furth in England, Wales and Ireland too.
At 2,025ft (617m), Laura said she chose Carn na h-Easgainn as a simple final ascent so family and friends could be there to celebrate her achievement.
Even her 89-year-old granny was able to be there on the summit near Tomatin, south of Inverness.
![A group of around 20 people pose around a concrete trig point on a grassy hilltop under cloudy skies. Several people hold walking poles and drinks, while one person sits in a folding chair in the foreground. The landscape stretches into the distance behind the group, suggesting a hillwalking or summit gathering.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/dc19/live/e2a7ebd0-9f03-11f1-8ab2-7700e58d1417.jpg)
Friends and family joined Laura at the summit of Carn na h-Easgainn
Laura said: "I left that one for last so that friends and family can join. I left them a super-easy one, it's an estate track all the way up.
"I'd been contacting estate owners and energy companies to find out who owned the land.
"With my gran turning 90 next month, my mum was granted access to drive her all the way to the summit, which is so, so special."
Laura is among the youngest women to complete the challenge, which can involve years of travelling to remote locations across the UK and Ireland.
![Person standing on a rocky mountain trail wearing a teal hiking top, backpack, and orange hiking shoes, holding a trekking pole. Expansive coastal landscape stretches into the distance with green fields, rugged hills, peninsulas, blue ocean, and dramatic low clouds overhead.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/a8cc/live/8602e690-9e2d-11f1-bed9-2f55a7feabfd.jpg)
Laura is one of the youngest women to complete the mammoth challenge
What mountains are in the 'full house' climbing challenge?
Scottish Mountaineering Club requires climbers to reach 1,072 summits across six different hill classifications to complete the "full house".
- Munros (282) - Scottish mountains over 3000ft (914m)
- Munro tops (226) - Mountains over 3000ft which do not have "sufficient separation" from their neighbouring peaks
- Corbetts (222) - Scottish peaks higher than 2500ft (762m) but less than 3000ft
- Grahams (219) - Scottish hills higher than 1968ft (600m) but under 2500ft (762m)
- Donalds (89) - Hills in the Scottish Lowlands over 2000ft (610m)
- Furths (34) - Mountains over 3,000ft (914m) in England, Wales and Ireland
Laura's effort involved countless early mornings and weekends away, remote routes, wild camping, and hiking in every kind of weather imaginable.
"The Corbetts are the most difficult," she told BBC Radio Scotland.
"There is a lot of pathless terrain, chest-deep bracken and your just cursing yourself and wondering why you can't just find another hobby.
"The Munros are quite defined pathwise, but you don't have to stick to a path you can make up your own routes as well.
"The more experience you get, the more confidence you have sitting with a map, creating your own routes and joining up hills that maybe other people wouldn't do."
![Person hiking uphill on a narrow mountain trail using trekking poles, surrounded by rolling heather-covered hills and distant snow-capped peaks under a clear blue sky.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1104/cpsprodpb/8bd8/live/16003e10-9e46-11f1-bb45-576721ee33bb.jpg)
Laura's feat involved countless weekends away following remote routes
Laura isn't a professional athlete. It has been a personal challenge for her alongside her everyday life in Glasgow as a property manager.
She has done it through sheer determination, commitment and a genuine love of Scotland's hills.
"I reckon I probably go out myself about 75 per cent of the time. You're in the most isolated parts of Scotland, you've got no phone reception.
"So I do check in with family and friends, give them my routes at the beginning of the walk, my ETA for when I finish.
"I check in to keep people informed so I don't have mountain rescue out looking for me."
Most skilled climbers
Just over 100 people are now registered with the Scottish Mountaineering Club as having accomplished the Full House feat.
In April last year, nine-year-old Kerry Blue Terrier Betty became the first dog to complete the challenge alongside her owner Shona Marshall.
The Scottish Mountaineering Club dates back to 1889 and its members have included many of Scotland's most skilled climbers.
Climbers must complete at least 50 Munros before they will be considered for membership, and have experience rock climbing and hiking in all weathers and seasons.
summary: Scottish climber Laura Baillie has become one of an elite group of about 100 people to complete the "full house" challenge of scaling all 1,072 UK and Irish peaks. The 38-year-old finished her final ascent at Carn na h-Easgainn in the Highlands, joined by family and friends including her 89-year-old granny. The demanding Scottish Mountaineering Club challenge encompasses 1,072 summits across six hill classifications, requiring years of travel and dedication alongside her everyday job.
key_points: Laura Baillie completed the "full house" of 1,072 summits across the UK and Ireland.
She is one of approximately 100 people and among the youngest women to achieve this milestone.
The challenge requires hikers to scale all Munros, Munro Tops, Corbetts, Grahams, Donalds, and Furths.
Her final ascent was up Carn na h-Easgainn, allowing her family, including her 89-year-old grandmother, to join her at the summit.

title: What’s on TV tonight and this week: The Terror, Mozart at the Proms, and more
author: Stephen Kelly; Gerard O'Donovan; Catherine Gee; Vicki Power
content:
![Dan Stevens in the third series of creepy anthology series The Terror](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/tv/2026/08/17/TELEMMGLPICT000498343864_17869784472690_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Dan Stevens in the third series of creepy anthology series The Terror](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/tv/2026/08/17/TELEMMGLPICT000498343864_17869784472690_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
What’s on TV tonight?
The Terror: Devil in Silver
Sky Atlantic, 9pm; all episodes are on Sky/NOW today
This horror tale is the third in an anthology series that started with 2018’s unforgettable chiller about a Victorian expedition to the Arctic. This run of the supernatural series, again executive produced by Ridley Scott, bears distinct echoes of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest. Set in the present day, it stars Downton Abbey’s Dan Stevens as Pepper, a New Yorker wrongly incarcerated in a psychiatric hospital after getting in a brawl. There he encounters the sharp end of an underfunded system where soiled mattresses are flipped over rather than replaced, and patients are drugged rather than rehabilitated to keep them compliant.
Even scarier are the many things at the so-called care facility that go bump in the night, introduced in the first episode as a horrific suicide, ominous noises and apparitions. Are menacing spirits truly inhabiting this hospital or an imagined byproduct of the hallucinogens being jabbed into Pepper’s arm? Stevens seizes his moment as the lucid in-patient navigating a broken system in which he’s lost his autonomy, with first-rate support from ER’s CCH Pounder and Stephen Root of Widow’s Bay fame as hospital staff. A strong sense of dread pervades the opening episode and – prepare yourself – results in proper jump scares.
Gymnastics: European Championships 2026
BBC Two, 12.45pm
Ten days of electrifying competition finish today at Arena Zagreb. Britain’s men will compete in the Juniors’ all-around final, followed by the Seniors’ team final. Having been pipped to gold by Ukraine in the Seniors’ two years ago in Italy, Team GB will be hoping to nab the top spot.
Mozart at the Proms
BBC Four, 8pm
Tonight’s crowd-pleaser sees chamber orchestra The Academy of St Martin in the Fields tackling exuberant works by Mozart, Elgar and Britten. French horn player Felix Klieser shines in a performance of Mozart’s Horn Concerto No 3 in E flat. Alongside these classics, bassoonist Amy Harman stars in the world premiere of Thea Musgrave’s new concerto, Out of the Darkness.
The Piano
Channel 4, 9pm
Tonight marks the culmination of the many weeks we’ve spent enraptured by the abilities of amateur pianists performing at Britain’s railway stations. Claudia Winkleman hosts the final concert at Birmingham Symphony Hall during which Mika and guest judge Alice Sara Ott will decide which pianist gave the finest performance of the night.
9/11: Reunited
National Geographic, 9pm
Marking 25 years since the attacks on the World Trade Centre, this three-part series reunites survivors and their rescuers in highly emotional meetings. Some want to say thank you and others to ask questions – the family of NYPD Emergency Service Unit officer John D’Allara meets the fireman who was with him in his final moments.
One Dollar
ITV, 11.20pm; all episodes are on ITVX today
Bearing strong Mare of Easttown vibes with its Pennsylvania rust belt setting and cop story narrative, this 10-part drama is built around a framework of following different locals who end up with a particular dollar bill. Tonight’s first recipient is steelworker Garrett Drimmer (Philip Ettinger), who turns up at work to a murder scene. VP
![Michael Sheen in Anniston, Alabama](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/tv/2026/08/13/TELEMMGLPICT000497645436_17866400014050_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqA7N2CxnJWnYI3tCbVBgu9T0aesusvN1TE7a0ddd_esI.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Buried with Michael Sheen
BBC One Wales/BBC Two, 9pm; all episodes are already on iPlayer
Last week’s jaw-dropping opening episode saw Michael Sheen and journalists Dan Ashby and Lucy Taylor take up the investigative work of farming consultant and whistleblower Douglas Gowan into the apparently deliberate dumping of highly dangerous chemical waste in the UK countryside. Waste that does not decompose. The company behind it is Monsanto – a US biotechnology corporation that was successfully sued in 1993 by residents in Anniston, Alabama for chemical contamination.
In this concluding part, the astonishing revelations come thick and fast – from the test that reveals one farm in Alvanley, Cheshire, has more than 2,000 times the normal amount of toxic PCB chemicals in the soil, to the discovery that PCBs are also present in the blood of some of the residents who live near the various dump sites. And then there are those who’ve suffered serious health problems. Michael Phillips played in a contaminated lagoon as a child and later developed a cancer in his shoulder that his surgeon said was so rare that it was as likely as winning the lottery. He also has a long list of childhood friends who have had cancer, including one, incredibly, with that same rare shoulder cancer.
Martin & Roman’s Irish Road Trip
Channel 4, 8pm
The father-and-son duo, made up of actor and Spandau Ballet star Martin Kemp and presenter Roman, have proven jolly holiday buddies – helped, of course, by Ireland’s beguiling landscape. In this third and final episode of their travelogue, they’re off to the craggy coastline of Northern Ireland and begin with a brave dip in the freezing sea, before spending the night in the country’s most haunted hotel.
The War Cabinet
PBS America, 8.30pm
Since Donald Trump’s second term began, the US military has become increasingly mired in conflicts in the Middle East, despite him campaigning on a promise to end the country’s involvement in foreign wars. This documentary utilises in-depth interviews with Trump’s allies, associates and critics to analyse how he has assembled his team of loyalists – and who the key players are.
Long Lost Family: Born Without Trace – What Happened Next
ITV1, 9pm
In 2022, Davina McCall and Nicky Campbell met Natasha, who had been abandoned as a baby in a south London hospital toilet. Their search revealed that Natasha had a full sister, Lee-Ann, who was also left in a hospital toilet 18 months earlier. This emotional episode finds out what has happened since. Plus, they return to the story of nurse Liz Deutsch, who was keen to search for more blood relatives.
Celebrity Hunted
Channel 4, 9pm
Five have been captured; now the remaining seven famous fugitives face the final battle to evade the crack team of professional hunters. One pair are soon collared, and another decides to make a very risky appearance at Bristol Pride. The final episode is tomorrow.
Secret Lives of Gypsy Wives 
Channel 4, 10pm; all episodes are already available to stream
Trewley Precious has become a TikTok sensation by pushing back against the strict traditional expectations of Gypsy women. In this final episode of the docuseries, she accompanies her big sister, Pearly, as she tries on fairy tale wedding dresses and plans her big day. Trewley, on the other hand, has a date with a non-Gypsy man – much to her family’s consternation. CG
![Ruth Goodman experiences life on the poorer end of the social spectrum in Tudor times](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/tv/2026/08/17/TELEMMGLPICT000498346151_17869856164710_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqfkvN-s6qkk_X3S-3OWGr2--ibwo9sdjTa8phqMEU1Jo.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The Tudors with Rob Rinder and Ruth Goodman
Channel 5, 9pm 
Having already done the Victorians, the Romans and the Georgians, this week our intrepid historical adventurers dip into the lives of rich and poor in Tudor times, taking the feverish summer of 1588 and the threat of the Spanish Armada as their subject matter. For Rinder, that means experiencing the life of a wealthy London merchant, Thomas Cordell, obliged by Elizabeth I to donate a couple of his highly valued trading ships to the war effort when the call to action comes. Goodman gets the less glamorous end of the stick, exploring the life of a struggling East End mother, Margaret Browne, whose husband William is away at sea aboard one of the gunships stationed in the English Channel preparing to repel the approaching Spanish fleet.
It’s all very accessible, albeit with AI-generated battle and crowd scenes fleshing out the fascinating facts and grim details. Rinder and Goodman work hard to ramp up the sense of jeopardy surrounding the imminent invasion and, ultimately, the significance of victory not just as an isolated moment of triumph but in laying the foundations for England’s future as a global power.
Race Against the Tide
BBC Two, 7.30pm
More fun on the beach at St Andrews as the sand-sculpting teams take on a new theme: “there’s no place like home”. How that translates into a green man, a handbag or a plaster rosette is anyone’s guess, but some of this week’s creations are certainly spectacular.
The Great British Sewing Bee
BBC One, 8pm
It’s music week, so what better pattern challenge to set the contestants than reproducing Madonna’s iconic Jean Paul Gaultier cone bra. There’s also a transformation task involving bedroom furnishings and the made-to-measure challenge is inspired by the disco culture of the 1970s.
Celebrity MasterChef
BBC One, 9pm
Week two of the heats and five more celebrities enter the arena: actors Nitin Ganatra and Donna Preston, Gladiator Emily Steel, YouTuber Tom Simons and ballet dancer Eric Underwood. Ahead of them lie a signature dish, a palate test and a tricky pappardelle cook-along with judge Giorgio Locatelli.
Emergency 24/7
BBC Two, 9pm
Two very different trauma cases test the expertise and judgement of the emergency team at Southmead Hospital. When a man whose leg has been severed after being hit by a train arrives in ED, his condition proves even more complicated than it looks. And there’s more, too, to a patient who presents with a deep wound but denies he’s been stabbed.
Little Bird
Sky Atlantic, 9pm & 10pm
The powerful drama set against the so-called Sixties Scoop scandal, when thousands of Canadian indigenous children were forcibly removed from their families and put up for adoption, continues. Having discovered more about her birth family and that her native name is Bezhig, Esther sets out to find her sister Dora. GO
![Mark Gatiss and guest star Jason Watkins](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/tv/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000498334386_17870480413670_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Bookish
U&Alibi, 8pm/9.15pm
What makes a crime drama cosy? Much like art or pornography, you tend to know it when you see it. Yet it can be broadly agreed that the recent boom favours quaint English aesthetics and simple, unchallenging mysteries. The kind of television that you can slip into after a long day, brain in jar. On paper, you would think that a period drama about a 1940s bookshop owner who solves murders by using his knowledge of literature would be equally disposable. But you know what they say – never judge a book by its cover.
Created by Sherlock co-creator Mark Gatiss, who also stars as closeted amateur sleuth Gabriel Book, the witty Bookish is the thinking viewer’s cosy crime. Consider tonight’s compelling two-part return, which revolves around the killing of charismatic medium Harold Sneed (Jason Watkins) during a séance. A delightfully absurd murder. Yet what elevates Bookish is how elegantly it marries its sillier elements with character and intellect. The show’s post-war setting, for instance, feels alive with the politics and culture of the time. Elsewhere, there is a fantastically written flashback scene where Book lays into “grief leech” Sneed, writing off mediums as “filthy, crooked, mendacious, disgusting pigs.”
The Airport Chaplain
Netflix
This big-hearted Australian drama follows unorthodox airport chaplain Tobias (Hugo Weaving) as he takes on the role of spiritual guide for weary travellers. It is a strange, multi-faceted job that puts him on a collision course with his fastidious new boss, played by The Pitt’s Shabana Azeez.
Rainbow Warrior
Sky Documentaries, 2am/10pm
In 1985, a ship belonging to Greenpeace was bombed in a New Zealand harbour. This nimble documentary tells the extraordinary story of the sinking, which was eventually traced back to the French intelligence service.
Kirstie and Phil’s Love It or List It: Brilliant Builds
Channel 4, 8pm
Kirstie Allsopp and Phil Spencer return for another series of couples debating whether to renovate or sell. Tonight’s retrospective episode is themed around builds that took advantage of wasted space. In Wolverhampton, for instance, Gordon and Suky transform their awkward layout with an open-plan redesign.
The Murder Detective
Channel 4, 9pm; all episodes are available to stream today
In 2019, journalist Lyra McKee was shot dead while observing a riot in Derry, Northern Ireland. This sobering three-part documentary, stripped across the week, follows the seven-year investigation into her murder. Tonight’s opening episode is also followed by The Never-Ending Murder at 10pm, which re-examines the 1991 disappearance of Coventry mum Nicola Payne.
The Great Wall of China with Dan Snow
Channel 5, 9pm
Historian Dan Snow travels from one end of the Great Wall of China to the other to find out how, and why, the wonder was built. Stretching some five and a half thousand miles, Snow describes the engineering involved as “mind-boggling”. And no, he stresses, you cannot see it from space. SK
![Howard Charles (left) stars as a champion boxer looking for revenge](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/tv/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000498345353_17870531888910_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Fightland
Sky Atlantic, from 9pm
Boxing meets organised crime in this violent new London-set drama from Curtis Jackson, better known as the rapper 50 Cent, who also writes the opening music. Tonight’s three (of eight) episodes introduce us to Duke Kilroy (Top Boy’s Howard Charles), whose stint as a champion boxer is only a few hours old when a tragic and violent development in a parking garage lands him in jail. Fast-forward seven years and Duke’s sprung from the nick and determined to wreak revenge on those who orchestrated his downfall – his former manager, crime kingpin Kingsley Marshall (a charismatic Nicholas Pinnock) and his family.
What unfolds is a story that shares DNA with 50 Cent’s US-set crime drama Power and its spin-offs, drawing us into a glamorous-but-dangerous world in which our antihero navigates a legitimate business operating alongside a nefarious one. Here, the wronged Duke travels both a revenge and a redemption arc as he rains violence on the bad guys while also displaying heart and smarts. The result is a gritty tale of pugilism and organised crime that feels familiar but has a gritty London edge and a solid lead in Charles, who never overplays Duke’s inner turmoil.
Live Test Cricket: England v Pakistan
Sky Sports Main Event, 10am
England and Pakistan resume their battle at the crease in the second Test match. Pakistan will likely be feeling confident, given their unusually strong record as visitors at Lord’s, having won more Test matches there (five) than the hosts (four). Catch the highlights on BBC Two at 7pm.
Dragons’ Den
BBC One, 8pm
The Dragons jostle for investment opportunities tonight when pitched businesses that include a fibre-rich snack food, an ad agency and a gardening gadget. Most impressive, however, is a line of girls’ and women’s cricket gear offered by the two teenagers who’ve designed and launched them – one of whom must leave mid-pitch to do her GCSEs.
The Big Deal With Steph McGovern
BBC Two, 8pm
This kinder iteration of The Apprentice, in which amateurs try their hands as art dealers, moves to hipster Margate. The five remaining pairs are tasked with finding artists whose prints and limited editions they’d like to sell at a pop-up fair. The series shines a light into a hidden corner of the art world and host McGovern keeps it fun.
Ludwig
BBC One, 9pm; all episodes are already on iPlayer
When a wedding ceilidh leads to murder, the cops ask Ludwig (David Mitchell) to figure out which guest could have stabbed the victim mid-dance. Meanwhile, Ludwig’s sister-in-law Lucy (Anna Maxwell Martin) ruffles feathers trying to track down her ex-husband.
A House Through Time
BBC Two, 9pm
The gripping social history series reaches the 20th century to find Calton Hill had been broken up into flats and was crammed with working-class families. Genial host David Olusoga talks us through the astonishing tale of one couple whose life included emigration, hardship and bigamy. VP
![Jo Martin, Samantha Bond and Cara Horgan in The Marlow Murder Club](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/tv/2026/08/18/TELEMMGLPICT000498780833_17870562037310_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqNJjoeBT78QIaYdkJdEY4CnGTJFJS74MYhNY6w3GNbO8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The Marlow Murder Club
BBC Two, 9pm 
Death in Paradise creator Robert Thorogood has become one of the most successful British writers of cosy crime. Adding to his TV success with the spin-off series Beyond Paradise and Return to Paradise, he also penned a bestselling series of novels in a similar idiom, the first of which is adapted here. Originally aired on U&Drama in 2024, it’s a classic middle-class mystery in the Agatha Christie tradition, set in the Thames-side town of Marlow, with Samantha Bond perfectly cast in the Marple-esque role of bored retiree/amateur sleuth Judith Potts.
When she hears a “kerfuffle” followed by a gunshot in her next-door neighbour’s sumptuous garden (she’s been fortunate enough to inherit a riverside Arts and Crafts mansion), the police’s refusal to take the matter seriously forces her to take the investigation into her own hands. It’s not long before she becomes a lovable thorn in the side of nice-but-inexperienced DS Tanika Malik (Natalie Dew), and she also convinces the vicar’s wife (Cara Horgan) and a local dog-walker (Jo Martin) to join her in her crime-fighting quest. It’s all terrifically silly and hugely enjoyable, and each of the two 90-minute episodes flies by. Concludes next week.
Meet the Owens
Amazon Prime Video
A new reality show follows a year in the eventful life of England’s former star striker Michael Owen, negotiating his post-footie career as a top-flight racehorse owner and breeder, while also juggling an entertainingly busy home life with his wife Louise, and their four children. A cut above the usual C-list celebrity fare.
Dark Matter
Apple TV
Apple’s sci-fi drama about a physicist (Joel Edgerton) forced to shuffle between endless alternate versions of his own life, desperate to get back to his wife (Jennifer Connelly) and son, returns for a second mind-bending run. This time the reunited Dessen family are on the run again; but at least they’re together, right?
Sister Boniface Mysteries
BBC One, 3pm 
Yet more cosy crime, as Lorna Watson is back for a third series of this Father Brown spin-off (also originally aired on U&Drama) as the wimple-wearing, Vespa-driving sleuth. When an actor doing a screen test for a spy film is killed by a scorpion, Boniface unearths a torrid tale of blackmail and infidelity.
The Met Orchestra at the Proms 
BBC Four, 7pm
Recorded highlights of Wednesday’s concert, the first ever Proms appearance by the New York Metropolitan Opera’s renowned Met Orchestra. Featuring soprano Elza van den Heever, it’s an all-Richard Strauss ticket, with the suite from Der Rosenkavalier, the closing scene from Salome and Ein Heldenleben to close.
The Rainmaker
ITV1, 9pm
Based on John Grisham’s 1996 thriller (which was adapted into a film a year later with Matt Damon), this legal drama stars Milo Callaghan as a hotshot young lawyer consigned to the world of ambulance chasing after he blows the opportunity of a lifetime on his first day at a big city law firm. GO
summary: This television highlights guide details a variety of programs airing tonight and this week, ranging from dramas and documentaries to entertainment and sports. Featured shows include the horror anthology series The Terror: Devil in Silver, the investigative documentary Buried, and the period crime drama Bookish. Other notable broadcasts cover historical series like The Tudors, emotional reunions on 9/11: Reunited, and the final stages of competitions like The Piano and Celebrity Hunted.
key_points: The Terror: Devil in Silver returns for its third season on Sky Atlantic, starring Dan Stevens as a man wrongly committed to a psychiatric hospital.
Buried concludes on BBC One Wales/BBC Two, examining whistleblower Douglas Gowan's findings regarding toxic chemical waste dumping by Monsanto in the UK.
Mark Gatiss stars in and created U&Alibi's Bookish, a 1940s-set period crime drama about a bookshop owner who solves murders using literature.
The European Gymnastics Championships conclude on BBC Two from Arena Zagreb, with Team GB competing in the Seniors' team final.
Channel 4's The Piano reaches its finale at Birmingham Symphony Hall, where judges will select the top amateur pianist.

title: Hayden Panettiere’s estranged mom slams Gayle King for ‘shameful’ comments
author: Tom Murray
content:
Hayden Panettiere’s mom slams Gayle King after host criticized her response to daughter’s death
![Hayden Panettiere’s mom slams Gayle King after host criticized her response to daughter’s death](<https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/23/15/14/Hayden-Panettiere-with-her-mom-Lesley-Vogel-and-Gayle-King.jpeg?quality=75&width=83&auto=webp 83w>)
Hayden Panettiere’s estranged mom slams Gayle King for ‘shameful’ comments
- Lesley Vogel, the mother of late actor Hayden Panettiere, criticized CBS Mornings host Gayle King for condemning her public statement following her daughter's death.
- Panettiere died at age 36 on August 16 in South Carolina, after which Vogel stated to NBC News that her daughter had sadly lost her way in the entertainment industry.
- King reacted on air to Vogel's comments by saying during the broadcast, “You know, guys, you read this and all I can think is, ‘Thanks, Mom, for nothing.’”
- “I was very, very hurt and deeply disappointed in the lack of professionalism, the lack of compassion in slamming someone who’s lost two children, without even a modicum of consideration,” Vogel told the Daily Mail about King’s criticism of her.
- Panettiere and Vogel were estranged at the time of the actor's death, following years of a strained relationship after Panettiere fired her mother as her manager at age 19.
summary: Lesley Vogel, the estranged mother of late actor Hayden Panettiere, criticized CBS Mornings host Gayle King for lacking compassion and professionalism. King had publicly condemned Vogel's statement to NBC News regarding her daughter's death at age 36, remarking, "Thanks, Mom, for nothing." Vogel expressed deep hurt over the comments, noting the lack of consideration for someone who has lost two children.
key_points: Hayden Panettiere passed away at the age of 36 on August 16 in South Carolina.
Following her death, Vogel publicly stated that her daughter had lost her way in the entertainment industry.
Gayle King criticized Vogel's remarks on air during a broadcast of CBS Mornings.
Vogel told the Daily Mail she was deeply hurt and disappointed by King's lack of compassion and professionalism.
Panettiere and Vogel were estranged at the time of the actor's death after a strained relationship that began when Panettiere fired her mother as her manager at age 19.

title: Former MCU Star Reveals Near-Casting As Professor X For X-Men Reboot
author: Andy Behbakht
content:
The Marvel Cinematic Universe franchise was close to bringing a former star back, but as a completely different character.
Robert Downey Jr. will be back in the MCU timeline this year, but not as Iron Man, as he will be playing Victor von Doom, a.k.a. Doctor Doom, in Avengers: Doomsday. But this isn't the first time Marvel Studios has brought an actor who has already been in the franchise for a different role, and one of their next projects was very close to repeating it.
In a new interview with The Hollywood Reporter, Tom Pelphrey confirmed the rumors that he had met with Marvel Studios about Professor X in the new X-Men movie. However, the role went to Christopher Abbott, with Pelphrey now opening up about not landing the part, which would have been his second time appearing in the MCU, after having previously played Ward Meachum in the Iron Fist series.
                        Tom Pelphrey: When it comes to opportunities like [Professor X], I am always of two minds. I am always a little torn in half. That’s a very long, serious commitment, and that makes me genuinely nervous because a lot of things can change in that time. So half of me thinks an experience like that could be cool and exciting, while the other half of me is a little worried about what could happen. But to be in the conversation for those kinds of roles, regardless of the specifics or how it plays out or why, it’s incredible.
To think about where I was ten years ago or even five years ago, it’s crazy the way this journey has unfolded. I don’t take any of it for granted. Like you said, I didn’t skip any steps to get here. I grinded for a long time, and my feet hit every rung on the ladder to get to where I am. I wouldn’t change any of it because I had to walk every single one of those steps to get here. I didn’t jump to the front of the line at any point or have one job that sent me into orbit. And thankfully so, honestly. To start from the bottom and then work my way up, I can see everything with a perspective that just leaves me feeling grateful.
Now, when one door closes, another door immediately opens, and it’s really changed the way I feel about certain projects. If something doesn’t work out and it isn’t perfect for everyone involved, great, because it’s probably perfect for someone else. That just means there’s something more perfect coming for me.
THR also asked the Task star how his younger self processed these types of experiences, as he went on to share that "when I was younger, I had much more of a zero-sum mentality. It has to be this, and I need to get this. So you’re either king of the universe for a while because you did get it, or you’re devastated because you didn’t get it. You feel like you’ve done something wrong if you didn’t get it, but it’s just not true. There are so many amazing opportunities, and to do one means you cannot do all the other ones. Every choice, in a way, is a sacrifice of all the other opportunities you’re not going to be able to do."
As the interview took place days prior to the X-Men cast being revealed at D23 2026, Pelphrey commented, "I tread lightly now. If something excites me — such as meeting a Louis Leterrier or a Jake Schreier [X-Men director], and I love them and enjoy talking with them — I’ll be like, Okay, let’s try this, but no guarantees ever. So that’s where I’m at now. It’s easy come, easy go."
While he didn't end up joining the X-Men movie, the Emmy-nominated actor still looks at those experiences as rewarding, nonetheless, as he stated the following.
                        Tom Pelphrey: You learn a lot from looking back. You see how something that felt like a disappointment in the moment led you to a greater good. But we can only see those things in the rear view. If you’re paying attention and you’ve lived long enough, you start to realize, I should stop thinking I always understand what the best thing for me is. I’m going to surrender my master plan and how it needs to be executed. I’m just going to stay open to whatever comes next.
So to have those [X-Men audition] experiences — and some of the other conversations and meetings I’ve had that haven’t been reported — it’s incredible. It’s been a good time. As much as I may have some talent and as much as I know I work hard, I am fortunate to be here. A lot of things have to go right at the right time to get here, so it’s all good.
If the Iron Fist alum had been tapped to play Charles Xavier, it would be the fourth time a major Marvel-Netflix star got cast as another character in the MCU. The first time this happened was in Captain America: Civil War when Luke Cage's Alfre Woodard showed up for a single scene, playing Miriam Sharpe, despite having joined the franchise as Mariah Stokes-Dillard in the Netflix drama.
Another Luke Cage veteran who was initially set to have a larger role in the MCU through his own solo film was Mahershala Ali. After playing the villainous Cornell Stokes, a.k.a. Cottonmouth, in season 1, he was going to portray Blade in a new reboot, which ended up getting stuck in development hell, with the Academy Award winner no longer attached to the project.
In 2025, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, who had already played Micro in The Punisher season 1, returned to the MCU, but this time as Ben Grimm, a.k.a. the Thing, in The Fantastic Four: First Steps. Despite this take on Marvel's First Family coming from Earth-828, the team is crossing over to Earth-616 in Avengers: Doomsday and will be back in Avengers: Secret Wars too.
The X-Men film opens in theaters on May 5, 2028.

title: Viral Cat in the Hat TikTok trend sparks fake videos and real fear
author: Anna Holligan
content:
![A person dressed Cat in the Hat character](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/683/cpsprodpb/e1cc/live/c24d6df0-9ef0-11f1-aed4-af6fe65bfcd6.jpg)
The Cat in the Hat, a character from the eponymous Dr Seuss book, has been depicted on screen multiple times, including photographed here on a US talk show
- Published
"He's so scary!" says 16-year-old Skye, recoiling at the mention of the Cat in the Hat.
Viral images purporting to show a life-sized version of the Dr Seuss character on the streets after dark have sparked fear and confusion among teenagers.
The posts, seen by millions, have convinced some young people that the character is real and that they might encounter it, prompting police forces in Ireland and the UK to issue statements confirming that the images and videos are fake.
"I was having a sleepover," Skye elaborates, "but everyone started watching Cat in the Hat videos. It was 3am. I wanted to go home. When I started walking down my friends' driveway, I got totally freaked out that the Cat in the Hat was going to jump out. I had to call my mum to pick me up."
A quick scroll through TikTok reveals numerous accounts, many of them created in the past few weeks, sharing photos and videos of an elusive black-and-white feline wearing the famous, towering, crooked red-and-white striped hat.
One post showing the original Cat in the Hat costume, accompanied by the caption "Help, what do I do?", has received 14.6m views in just three weeks.
The comments add to the sense of frenzy, with followers asking, "Why is he taxidermied?" Others zoom in on parts of the costume and post conspiracy theories about Mike Myers, who played the character in the 2003 film, being trapped inside.
Another popular account set up this week, posts videos of a real person dressed in a cat in the hat costume, dancing, with captions like "Kent I'm coming. lock your doors." Other users are sharing the videos, adding their own captions and locations across the UK.
Many of the AI generated images have been centred on the Irish counties of Limerick and Wexford, where shaky videos purportedly showed the character wandering through the streets, causing alarm and confusion among residents.
In Wexford, the local GardaÃ (police force) quickly dismissed the sightings as fake and confirmed that the images had been generated using artificial intelligence.
![The full image of the ai-generated Cat in the Hat image shared by Wexford Garda which includes the label "AI GENERATED".](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/673/cpsprodpb/cc4c/live/1b80a410-9f0e-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.png)
That has not stopped the pictures and videos from spreading online - along with unverified claims posted without evidence that the Cat in the Hat has been involved in violent assaults.
"I low-key wanna go meet himâ¦" says 14-year-old Lily, who heard that the Cat in the Hat had arranged a "meet and greet", inviting local TikTok followers to come to the woods in Galashiels, a small town in the Scottish Borders.
Her mother was horrified by the prospect.
"You are not going to meet anyone in the woods in the middle of the night!" she told her.
There is a point at which viral dancing videos and AI-generated clips of the Cat in the Hat become something potentially more sinister, with real-world consequences beyond their impact on teenage imaginations.
In England, South Yorkshire Police has denied social media claims that a 'killer Cat in the Hat' has been spotted. Posts about the alleged sightings have attracted hundreds of thousands of views on TikTok.
There is also a fake Facebook post claiming to be from Yorkshire Police - no force with that name actually exists - and suggesting that the force is taking the rumoured sighting seriously.
In response, a South Yorkshire Police spokesperson said: "If you do see posts online providing policing updates and advice, please check that they are from an official policing account. The cat is not out of the hat on this oneâ¦ Please don't believe everything you read on social media."
As with so many trends driven by TikTok, comedic reaction and spoofery is what will be appearing right now on many people's For You page.
In recent days, depending largely on what your algorithm serves up, you may be seeing nearly as many people in Cat in the Hat costumes dancing to Beyonce as those stalking the streets. There are several jokey videos depicting police chasing human sized cats, and Scottish drag performer Ellie Diamond has issued a video declaring that she is not the Cat in the Hat killer.
And Irish TikTok star Garron Noone said on one post that it should have been obvious it was a hoax "because even the most soulless, evil, vicious monster" would be "traumatised looking in the window of a Wexford person".
Snapchat filters and images shared in group chats suggest that many teenagers - and those not so young - are simply having harmless fun with the trend.
But some do remain perturbed, including another teenager in the Scottish borders, 16-year-old Ellie, who says: "I was so scared of him when I was little," Ellie confides. "Now it's like he's actually come to life to haunt me."
![Cat in the Hat Snapchat filter](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1056/cpsprodpb/9f25/live/ee8915c0-9f1f-11f1-b2a2-8945a27a2843.jpg)
Not all Cat in the Hats are scary - this one is my brother Nicholas demonstrating the Snapchat filter
A post on X that appears to have accelerated the current viral phenomenon appears to have been made on 8 August, by DiscussingFilm, when the pop culture site posted that the original costume was being auctioned off by Propstore.
The post has 10 million views. , externalComments describe it as "nightmare fuel" and "genuinely haunting", suggesting it had been pulled from a 'cursed attic'.
The lot is scheduled to be sold, external on Wednesday as part of an auction of 1,400 pieces of film and TV memorabilia and is predicted to fetch a price of up to $24,000 (Â£17,500).
![A screengrab of the original Cat in the Hat suit from the 2003 Mike Myers film, it features a tall red and white top hat and a red tie and is showing noticeable signs of disrepair.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/365/cpsprodpb/e7b0/live/7bb2d450-9f0b-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
The costume, which has shown noticeable signs of disrepair, was put up for auction by online retailer Propstore for $12,000-$24,000
Emily, a mother in Scotland, says the trend reminds her of the "Momo Challenge", a notorious internet hoax and digital urban legend. At the time, fact-checkers and authorities found no verified evidence linking the meme to children harming themselves, although the frightening images were still capable of causing distress.
"I'm not worried about my daughters, but there could be people with bad intentions who might take advantage of this trend to manipulate teenagers."
For now, the evidence points not to a real, roaming Cat in the Hat, but to a rapidly evolving online story built from an auctioned film costume, people in costume, AI-generated material and unverified posts.
Whether the claims began as a joke or were deliberately designed to frighten and manipulate, the advice from police is the same: pause before sharing, check the original source and date, look for confirmation from official police accounts, and treat invitations to meet strangers, especially at night or in isolated places, as a serious warning sign.
The rapidly evolving trend terrorising or tantalising teenagers on TikTok across the UK and Ireland is a reminder that online fear can quickly spill into the real world.
Additional reporting by John Hand
summary: A viral TikTok trend featuring AI-generated images and videos of a life-sized Cat in the Hat character has sparked fear and confusion among teenagers in the UK and Ireland. Police forces in Ireland and the UK have confirmed the sightings are fake and cautioned the public against believing unverified social media claims. The trend was partly accelerated by online attention surrounding the auction of the original film costume by Propstore.
key_points: Viral AI-generated images and videos on TikTok have convinced some teenagers that a life-sized Cat in the Hat is roaming the streets at night.
Police forces in Ireland and the UK, including Wexford Garda and South Yorkshire Police, have issued statements confirming the sightings are fake.
Unverified social media claims have falsely linked the fictional character to violent assaults and fake police warnings.
The online phenomenon was accelerated by interest in the original 2003 film costume being put up for auction by Propstore with an estimated price of up to $24,000.

title: Emily Atack hires McDonald’s van for ‘perfect’ wedding
author: Telegraph Reporters
content:
![Emily Atack marries partner Alistair Garner](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499322891_17875080765150_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqDfH7F16Xk0VA0Enc8HeGHn4ihL9D5G77hk2Gx25ScXg.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Emily Atack marries partner Alistair Garner](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499322891_17875080765150_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqDfH7F16Xk0VA0Enc8HeGHn4ihL9D5G77hk2Gx25ScXg.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Emily Atack has revealed that she hired a personalised McDonald’s van serving McFlurries during her “perfect” wedding to her partner of three years.
The Rivals star, 36, and her partner Alistair Garner, a scientist, married at the weekend.
She shared a post on Instagram, which read: “Yesterday we officially got married among close family and friends. It was absolutely perfect.
“I can’t believe we get to do all that again in a few weeks time. Christ, we have fun don’t we @dralistairgarner.”
![Emily Atack at her wedding](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499333715_17875092112540_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqXHe8ZIM0U4GF9WyVFAYFLEWy_sGK6oioMu5BzggyGUY.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
It has been reported that the second ceremony will take place in Spain next month.
A source previously told The Sun: “Emily has been going to Spain with her family on holiday ever since she was a child and loves the idea of getting married there. She and Alistair adore the stunning countryside there, and guaranteed sun is a bonus.”
Atack shared a selection of photos from the wedding, including one of the couple walking through a crowd of guests as they were showered in confetti.
![The McDonald's van at Emily Atack's wedding](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499333714_17875090413090_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqr6KNllb_vRHMhZOYxFcLXxD-pJQUiO0r3TxuD8Gp7X8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Another post on her Instagram showed a McDonald’s van serving McFlurries next to a sign saying “Mr and Mrs Garner”.
Before the ceremony, the actress revealed that children would not be invited, telling The Romesh Ranganathan Show podcast: “We’re being kind to our friends and making sure that people don’t have to worry too much about paying for lots of things, but we have said no kids at the wedding.
“I’m surprised by how many people are happy about that. I thought I’d get a lot of people kicking off.”
![Emily Atack and Alistair Garner kiss](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499322894_17875092682870_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqWe-Z1SiZYGAqkFat3OBdA5dpFBgxV75HFcFnHhXRNew.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The actress announced their engagement in July last year, sharing a photo of the couple cuddling, which she captioned: “It’s Friday, I’m in love” alongside three ring emojis. They had a son, Barney James Garner, now two, in June 2024.
Atack stars as Sarah Stratton in the award-winning Disney+ show Rivals, which is based on Jilly Cooper’s novels and follows the high-stakes world of British television against the backdrop of the 1980s Cotswolds countryside.
She rose to fame as a teenager playing Charlotte Hinchcliffe on The Inbetweeners and appeared on reality shows including Dancing on Ice and I’m a Celebrity… Get Me Out of Here!
summary: Actress Emily Atack and her partner, scientist Alistair Garner, married over the weekend in front of close family and friends. The couple celebrated their "perfect" wedding with a personalised McDonald's van that served McFlurries. A second ceremony is reportedly planned to take place in Spain next month.
key_points: Emily Atack married her partner Alistair Garner after three years together.
The wedding featured a personalised McDonald's van serving McFlurries.
A second wedding ceremony is reported to take place in Spain next month.
The couple welcomed their son, Barney James Garner, in June 2024.
Children were not invited to the wedding ceremony.

title: Royals put on united front at church in Scotland
author: Telegraph Reporters
content:
![Prince and Princess of Wales driving to the church](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499295465_17874841332930_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqjPAKgJRxicfimPcewMJ7fNHhMh81Y8GqX3ipA8YMo0k.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Prince and Princess of Wales driving to the church](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499295465_17874841332930_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqjPAKgJRxicfimPcewMJ7fNHhMh81Y8GqX3ipA8YMo0k.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
The Royal family has appeared together for the first time since the news broke that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are relocating to the UK.
On Sunday morning, the King and Queen were pictured attending a church service near the Balmoral estate alongside the Prince and Princess of Wales and their three children.
The family’s united front comes days after The Telegraph revealed the Sussexes were returning to the UK later this month, and their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, were enrolled at a British school to start in September.
![The King and Queen arriving at Crathie Kirk](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499295624_17874841718930_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
![Queen Camilla wore green, with a feather in her hat, for the first church service of the monarchs' summer stay at Balmoral](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499298811_17874891874671_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqB9TNGSg3mw1zIYGf6IZil15NUcTKNHKqy85KLqtvPLE.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The King is said to be pleased to have the opportunity to see more of the family regularly, both in a private and personal capacity.
The monarch, who was informed of the couple’s plans last Sunday, officially began his summer residence at the Royal family’s Scottish home on Monday.
He was welcomed in a formal ceremony at Balmoral by the Balaklava Company, the 5th Battalion, Royal Regiment of Scotland. The same troops provided a guard of honour on Sunday as members of his extended family arrived at the Crathie Kirk church in Aberdeenshire.
The Prince and Princess of Wales, who arrived at Balmoral earlier this week, were accompanied by their three children, Prince George, 13, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, 8.
Their Majesties are also hosting the Princess Royal and her husband Sir Tim Laurence, as well as the Duke of Edinburgh and his daughter, Lady Louise, who recently graduated from St Andrew’s University and is beginning a gap year.
![Troops from the Balaklava Company formed a guard of honour for the royal party](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499296630_17874891889560_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Troops from the Balaklava Company lined up on both sides of the driveway leading to the church to welcome the family as a fleet of cars brought the royal occupants to the door.
A crowd of onlookers had gathered outside the front of the church to witness their arrival at the small Church of Scotland parish kirk, which is their regular place of worship when they are at Balmoral, and where Elizabeth II would regularly attend services.
![The Princess Royal's party arriving at Crathie](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499295958_17874841722102_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The Telegraph reported this week that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex will not be guaranteed an invitation to Royal family gatherings, including the traditional summer invitation to Balmoral and Christmas at Sandringham, despite their return to Britain.
All family members’ attendance at such gatherings, including the annual holiday in Scotland and Christmas at Sandringham, is by personal invitation from the King.
The Sussexes are not expected to join the Balmoral holiday this year because of the logistics of their move, although it has not been ruled out.
The monarch has previously emphasised how his younger son, his wife and children, will always be members of his family. In his first address to the nation upon his ascension to the throne, he spoke of his love for Harry and Meghan as they “continue to build their lives overseas”.
The Duke and Duchess are expected to maintain their status as non-working royals, described by Palace sources as the terms that they “signed up to” under Elizabeth II.
The King and Prince William are said to agree on upholding the late Queen’s wishes, in which she said that a life of public service is “not possible” without official duties.
summary: Members of the Royal family attended a Sunday church service near the Balmoral estate in Scotland, marking their first public appearance together since news of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex relocating to the UK. The King and Queen, along with the Prince and Princess of Wales and their three children, were among those present at Crathie Kirk. The gathering takes place as the King begins his summer residence at Balmoral, where he is hosting several members of the extended family.
key_points: The Royal family put on a united front at Crathie Kirk near the Balmoral estate in Scotland.
The appearance follows the announcement that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are returning to live in the UK.
The King is hosting multiple family members during his summer residence at Balmoral, including the Prince and Princess of Wales.
Troops from the Balaklava Company formed a guard of honour for the royal party arriving at the church.

title: Hayden Panettiere’s mom lashes out at Gayle King over ‘shameful’ attacks on her
author: Tom Murray
content:
Hayden Panettiere’s estranged mother, Lesley Vogel, has hit back at Gayle King after the CBS Mornings host criticized her response to her daughter’s death.
The Heroes star died August 16 after being found in cardiac arrest at a Greenville, South Carolina, apartment. She was 36.
“I was very, very hurt and deeply disappointed in the lack of professionalism, the lack of compassion in slamming someone who’s lost two children, without even a modicum of consideration,” Vogel told the Daily Mail about King’s criticism of her.
“No one reached out to me before,” she added. “It’s shameful. It’s unconscionable to me.”
The Independent has contacted King’s representatives for comment.
![Hayden Panettiere’s mother, Lesley Vogel (center), hit back at Gayle King (right) after the TV host criticized her reaction to Panettiere’s death](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/23/15/14/Hayden-Panettiere-with-her-mom-Lesley-Vogel-and-Gayle-King.jpeg)
After Panettiere’s death, Vogel told NBC News: “I think Hayden was an amazingly talented person in so many departments and I think young people who grow up in the entertainment industry — it is a struggle and it's a very challenging industry and it’s not unusual for them to sadly find the wrong path.
“I think it becomes very difficult to be true to yourself, and I think Hayden sadly lost her way, and I wish it were different,” Vogel continued. “I wish she had stayed true to herself because she had many incredible attributes.”
She concluded: “I just feel that she’s with her brother and they’re at peace.” Panettiere’s younger brother Jansen died from an enlarged heart in 2023 at the age of 28.
On CBS Mornings, King lashed out at Vogel’s statement.
“You know, guys, you read this and all I can think is, ‘Thanks, Mom, for nothing,’” she said during the broadcast.
“It makes me so sad of the opportunity that you have after your daughter’s death that that’s what you choose to leave us with,” King said.
The Nashville star spoke openly about her strained relationship with her mother, who was her manager during her rise to fame as a child star. The two were estranged at the time of Panettiere’s death, and the actor had told podcaster Jay Shetty in May that Vogel “didn’t care to have a relationship with me.”
Vogel served as Panettiere’s manager from the time she was just an infant.
The actor opened up about her relationship with her mother in an interview with The Independent in May.
“She’s a very complex person,” Panettiere said. “I don’t want to offend anybody, or drag anybody, or hurt anyone’s feelings. But I knew that if I wasn’t honest about my relationship with her, I wouldn’t be being honest at all. She’s a huge part of the person I am today.”
Panettiere cut professional ties with Vogel at the age of 19, while working on Heroes. In her memoir, released earlier this year, she said she asked Vogel to meet her in her trailer and begged her to just be her mother.
“All I wanted was a dynamic that didn’t involve contracts, producers, boho tops, or drinking wine at industry parties,” she wrote.
Vogel, Panettiere claimed, “picked up her purse, clenched her jaw, and looked straight at me. ‘You owe me,’ she answered. Then she turned around and walked out of my trailer ... I knew I’d done the right thing, but I sensed something in me had died.”
summary: Hayden Panettiere's estranged mother, Lesley Vogel, has criticized Gayle King for lacking professionalism and compassion after the CBS Mornings host condemned Vogel's public remarks about her daughter's death. Panettiere passed away at age 36 following a history of a strained relationship with Vogel, who previously served as her manager. Vogel expressed deep hurt that King criticized her without reaching out or considering that she has lost two children.
key_points: Lesley Vogel hit back at Gayle King for criticizing her public response to Hayden Panettiere's death.
King had called Vogel's remarks regarding her late daughter 'shameful' and stated, 'Thanks, Mom, for nothing' on CBS Mornings.
Vogel stated that King lacked compassion and professionalism by attacking someone who has lost two children without contacting her first.
Panettiere and her mother had a publicly strained relationship, and the actor had been estranged from Vogel at the time of her death.

title: Anna Paquin mourns ‘untimely ends’ of multiple child actors
author: Louis Chilton
content:
Anna Paquin calls out practice of child acting as she pays tribute to Hayden Panettiere: ‘We were not protected’
![Anna Paquin calls out practice of child acting as she pays tribute to Hayden Panettiere: ‘We were not protected’](<https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/22/9/03/MixCollage-22-Aug-2026-10-36-AM-9038.jpeg?quality=75&width=83&auto=webp 83w>)
Anna Paquin mourns ‘untimely ends’ of multiple child actors after Hayden Panettiere’s death
- Former child star Anna Paquin has condemned the treatment of young female performers following the death of Heroes and Nashville actor Hayden Panettiere at the age of 36.
- Paquin, who won an Oscar at 11 for her role in The Piano, wrote on Instagram: “It’s not a coincidence that so many former, specifically pre-sexualized female, child ‘stars’ have profoundly sad lives and untimely ends.”
- She added: “We were not as protected by the ‘systems’ that look great on paper as we are supposed to be.”
- Paquin highlighted the untimely deaths of other former child actors, including Michelle Trachtenberg and Daveigh Chase.
- Actor Rose McGowan also spoke out against child acting following Panettiere's death, urging parents not to put children into show business.
summary: Former child star Anna Paquin criticized the child acting industry following the death of actor Hayden Panettiere at age 36. Paquin highlighted the untimely deaths of multiple former child actors, including Michelle Trachtenberg and Daveigh Chase, and stated that young performers were not adequately protected. Actor Rose McGowan also spoke out against the industry, urging parents to keep their children out of show business.
key_points: Anna Paquin condemned the treatment of young female performers following Hayden Panettiere's death at age 36.
Paquin stated that pre-sexualized female child stars often face profoundly sad lives and untimely ends due to a lack of protection.
Paquin noted the untimely deaths of other former child actors, such as Michelle Trachtenberg and Daveigh Chase.
Actor Rose McGowan also spoke out, urging parents not to put their children into the show business industry.

title: “The new Grantchester”: 7 “outstanding” TV shows to watch this week on ITV, Netflix, the BBC and more
author: Nathalie Whittle
content:
A new week is here and if you’ve got no interest in wading through the TV schedules for something good to watch, we’ve come to your rescue. We’ve previewed all of this week’s new shows to bring you 7 that we consider to be absolutely outstanding.
From the return of what we’re calling the new Grantchester to two huge shows that are bringing Vicky McClure and Suranne Jones back to our screens, we’ve got something for every mood. So, take a moment to relax with our pick of the 7 best shows to watch this week on ITV, Netflix, the BBC and more.
Bookish
Mark Gatiss’s cosy crime series earned an army of fans when it arrived on U&Alibi last July, so of course it’s returning for a second run. Gabriel Book (Gatiss) is back in his bookshop in Archangel Lane and he’s drawn into the world of spiritualism when he’s asked to help solve an unusual case involving medium, Harold Sneed (Jason Watkins). He also has a puzzling murder at a gentleman’s outfitters to solve, as well as a thieving Duchess (played by Miranda Richardson) to contend with. With a third series already commissioned and a Christmas special also on the way, we’re calling it the new Grantchester. Series 2 is arriving on U&Alibi at 8pm on Wednesday 26th August.
Fightland
Sky is bringing us something a bit different this week in the form of boxing drama Fightland. Set and filmed in London, the series takes us into the world of British-born boxer Duke Kilroy (Howard Charles) who’s on a quest for revenge. Why? Well, on the night he became world heavyweight champion, a vicious assault left his brother, Calvin, dead, and his reaction in the aftermath resulted in him spending 8 years in a US prison. His eventual release, therefore, can only mean one thing: vengeance. Arriving on Sky Atlantic and NOW at 9pm on Thursday 27th August.
The Rainmaker
ITV has picked up this adaptation of John Grisham’s bestselling legal thriller and it’s not hard to see why. The 10-part series follows newly qualified lawyer Rudy Baylor (Milo Callaghan) who enters the legal world full of wide-eyed optimism – only to realise he’s in for a difficult ride. Having been fired by the unscrupulous and powerful Leo Drummond (John Slattery), he lands at an underdog firm with the hope of starting afresh - until a deeply buried conspiracy means he must go head-to-head with his old boss. Arriving on ITVX on Friday 28th August.
The Whisper Man
Netflix’s creepy new abduction drama introduces us to widowed crime writer, Tom Kennedy (Adam Scott), who moves to a new town for a fresh start with his eight-year-old son, Jake. When Jake vanishes into thin air, Tom is forced to reach out to his estranged dad and retired detective Peter Willis (Robert De Niro) for help, who discovers a link between Jake’s disappearance and a decades-old case of a convicted serial killer nicknamed “The Whisper Man”. The latter, however, was supposedly imprisoned years ago - so can it really be him? Arriving on Netflix on Friday 28th August.
Dark Matter
Series 1 of this mind-bending thriller followed Jason Dessen (Joel Edgerton), a physicist, professor and family man who - one night while walking home on the streets of Chicago - was abducted into an alternate version of his life. Now, having fought his way back to his true family, the Dessens are settling into a quiet life in a world that finally seems safe - that is, until the unimaginable forces them to run once again. Series 2 is arriving on Apple TV on Friday 28th August.
Trigger Point
Almost a year on from the series 2 finale, Vicky McClure is back as bomb disposal operative Lana Washington who dedicates herself to keeping the capital safe – and she’s in for her biggest challenge yet. She and her team are coming up against an unprecedented threat which, according to guest star Julie Graham - who plays Commander Nia Quentin - is “the biggest terror attack this country’s seen”. Eek! Series 4 is arriving on ITV1 and ITVX at 9pm on Sunday 30th August.
Vigil
On its release in 2021, Vigil became one of the BBC’s most-watched new dramas - for good reason! Suranne Jones plays the intelligent and resilient DCI Amy Silva, who in series 1 is tasked with investigating the suspicious death of a crew member on board the HMS Vigil submarine. Series 2 saw her sent to a Middle Eastern military base and now, she’s off to a remote Arctic research station, where a member of a covert British special forces mission has been shot dead. We can’t wait! Series 3 is arriving on BBC One and BBC iPlayer at 9pm on Sunday 30th August.
summary: A curated selection of seven television shows is highlighting upcoming releases across various networks and streaming platforms for the week. The featured lineup includes returning fan-favorite crime dramas, thrilling legal adaptations, and new seasons of major hits starring actors such as Vicky McClure and Suranne Jones. These programs span genres from cosy mysteries and boxing revenge stories to high-stakes political thrillers and sci-fi.
key_points: Mark Gatiss's cosy crime series 'Bookish' returns for its second season on U&Alibi on August 26.
Sky Atlantic and NOW are releasing the boxing drama 'Fightland' on August 27, following a boxer seeking revenge.
ITV and Netflix are introducing new adaptations and thrillers including 'The Rainmaker' and 'The Whisper Man' on August 28.
Popular dramas 'Trigger Point' and 'Vigil' are returning for new series on ITV and the BBC respectively at the end of the week.

title: The Office’s Lucy Davis ‘grateful’ for support after cancer diagnosis
author: Telegraph Reporters
content:
![Lucy Davis announced that she had incurable stage-four cancer on Aug 11](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499218219_17874864960600_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq13fR010OlVR1q5kIHbAg0sSGsf1MRXWWC7NY2csU23E.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Lucy Davis announced that she had incurable stage-four cancer on Aug 11](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499218219_17874864960600_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq13fR010OlVR1q5kIHbAg0sSGsf1MRXWWC7NY2csU23E.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Lucy Davis, the actress, has said she is grateful for the support she has received since revealing she has incurable breast cancer.
The 53-year-old star of The Office appeared at the For The Love of Fantasy and Sci-Fi convention at Excel London on Saturday to talk about Shaun of the Dead, the 2004 zombie comedy in which she played Dianne.
It was her first public appearance since announcing on Aug 11 that she had incurable stage-four cancer that had metastasised to her bones since a diagnosis a year and a half ago.
Speaking on a panel with Edgar Wright, the film’s director, and Simon Pegg, its main character, Davis thanked an audience of hundreds for their support.
![She sits behind a desk](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000498041452_17874752193620_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqioymxFNOxszPImVXwX3fiHmgdWlwnpW8RUbJvbVjxBY.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Saying she had been signing autographs and posing for photographs at the convention, she added: “It’s like this whole second family you never knew you had, everyone is like a community, friendly, supportive of not only us but you guys and each other.
“We need a bit more niceness in the world, so I’m grateful.”
Davis, whose father is Jasper Carrott the comedian, needed assistance to get on and off the stage for the 30-minute appearance. She was not asked directly about her health.
![A large cast photo on set](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000489584417_17874752434300_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq3Z7i_2nUjuO-XXgVmfiyhMbHf4DfgeegiUIPq8ZyLgk.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Best known for playing receptionist Dawn Tinsley in Ricky Gervais’s hit BBC series The Office, Davis was given a round of applause when asked for advice about getting into the film industry.
She said: “Don’t let anyone tell you you can’t do or be anything you want to do or be. We all grow up with a different life with a different world telling us we all have limitations.
“None of us do, our only limitations are things that we think are limiting. We can do anything, or be anybody, and don’t apologise for that.”
Davis thanked fans two days after she announced her condition, which has spread to her spine, right hip and ribs, and said it was “too late” for chemotherapy.
In a post on Instagram, she said: “Ok, so the last two days have been utterly overwhelming, in that I had zero idea my cancer post would have the attention it did.
“Truly, I am in shock. That said, thank you to everyone for the tremendous amount of kindness and support you have sent me. Good grief it was emotional.”
![She poses in a cocktail dress](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000498036450_17874752717380_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq_MBhvjUqhIfRd2_dxg_gJw-sBi3FXIEymT6xV4gqOJY.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Fans in the audience on Saturday told the actress “I love you so much” and heard her tell stories of filming Shaun of the Dead with a cast that included Nick Frost, Dylan Moran and Bill Nighy.
She spoke of being driven home in Los Angeles by Quentin Tarantino, being recognised after The Office first aired, and the difficulty of filming with seven cast members in a car.
When asked for her favourite memories on set, she said: “Comradery. In terms of actually filming, I loved when we all pretended to be zombies and walked across the square. It was like being naughty school kids.
“Our first week of filming, we were all in the car, Nick was driving, and it was almost like the seven stages of grief in those few days, I’d been sat on Dylan’s lap for so long.
“At one point it all got really quiet and suddenly out of nowhere Bill Nighy went ‘let’s all get into our pyjamas and out of our normal clothes’ and just stopped talking. We all loved it, but couldn’t express it!
“It was a fun time, we went a bit mad!”
summary: Actress Lucy Davis has expressed gratitude for the overwhelming support she has received since announcing she has incurable stage-four breast cancer. Making her first public appearance at the For The Love of Fantasy and Sci-Fi convention, she thanked fans and spoke alongside her Shaun of the Dead co-stars. Davis is best known for her roles in Shaun of the Dead and as Dawn Tinsley in The Office.
key_points: Lucy Davis made her first public appearance since revealing her incurable stage-four cancer diagnosis on August 11.
She appeared at the Excel London convention alongside director Edgar Wright and actor Simon Pegg to discuss Shaun of the Dead.
Davis thanked hundreds of fans in attendance for their kindness and sense of community support.
She shared behind-the-scenes memories from the 2004 zombie comedy and offered words of encouragement to aspiring filmmakers.

title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
author: Pauline McLean
content:
![Two men in their 50s either side of a poster for The Wicker Man outside a cinema. Dominic, on the left, is in a tweed suit and has glasses and thick hair. Justin (right) is in a cord suit and has a beard. They are smiling and pointing at the poster.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/746/cpsprodpb/158f/live/ed9a2d40-9ef0-11f1-aed4-af6fe65bfcd6.jpg)
Dominic and Justin Hardy embraced the legacy of their father's film The Wicker Man
- Published
Robin Hardy always envisaged his iconic 1973 folk horror film The Wicker Man as the first part of a trilogy.
The Wicker Tree, released in 2011, brought him closer to that ambition, but his death in 2016 at the age of 86 left the project incomplete.
Now his sons, Justin and Dominic, have been able to complete their father's trilogy, after finding a script for the final film.
Wrath of the Gods has its premiere at the FrightFest horror festival in London, external on Friday, a family dream made possible thanks to the surprise discovery of some long-lost family archive.
"The person who bought Justin's old family home said they'd discovered six sacks of letters, scripts and other material pertaining to Robin Hardy and The Wicker Man in the attic," says Dominic, an art historian at the University of Quebec in Montreal.
"Justin's first instinct was to burn them, but we couldn't ignore this original source material. Although we left it unopened for six months or more."
The archive haul included papers, scripts and storyboards, but it also shed light on the long shadow cast by The Wicker Man.
The film holds a unique place in British cinema history. It was shot at a time when the UK industry was in crisis. Its financial backers were struggling and its stars - including horror legend Christopher Lee - had to go without being paid to get it finished.
It was set on a Hebridean island in spring but was shot in Galloway in the autumn and early winter. On its release, it was largely buried as a second feature. There were competing edits and tales of missing material, some of which was said to be literally buried in the supporting columns of a motorway.
But the film's reputation grew. Lee considered it one of his finest films, featuring one of his finest performances. Its off-kilter tone and genuinely disturbing climax made it a favourite for horror fans.
By the time the BBC launched the cult cinema series Moviedrome in 1988, external, there was only one choice for opening night - the premiere of a previously unseen edit of The Wicker Man.
![The Wicker Man. A large wicker man standing in a field with four people standing beside it with torches, waiting to set it alight.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/70f0/live/dfdcd640-9e45-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
The Wicker Man itself was built on a cliff in Galloway
![A bunch of men in Viking outfits and burning torches march in a line. Some are in modern dress too.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/53ed/live/39e9a020-9e3a-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Wrath of The Gods draws on Viking and Shetland mythology
The film's troubled production was mirrored by the troubles it brought Robin Hardy and his family.
It bankrupted the director, and he abandoned Justin's mother Caroline, leaving her with all his debts.
He went on to marry four more times, and had eight children in all.
Justin and Dominic talk about their complicated relationship with the film in the 2024 book and documentary Children Of The Wicker Man.
The recently unearthed archive included a script for that proposed third and final film, Wrath of the Gods, as well as details of how their father had come up with the idea.
"He had had been in an airplane and had a turn because his heart medication wasn't working," says Dominic.
"He had to land in Reykjavik and spend a week recuperating, and he came back with this idea of a theme park around an extinct volcano in Iceland where the Norse gods get upset and mayhem ensues.
"And then he decided it ought to be set in Shetland because of the other parts of the trilogy."
Justin, an Emmy and BAFTA-nominated director, worked on the idea with Dominic. They came up with their own original story, in which a young grieving widow returns to the island of Hel to bury her late husband after his suicide.
She's cast out by the community, who look on her as a symbol of evil and bad luck. When children start going missing, the island is forced to confront its own complex history.
![A black and white photo showing a young boy and girl sitting on their father's knee in an armchair in front of a Christmas tree. The three are smiling.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/1898/live/e3509d10-9e41-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.png)
Justin Hardy (left) was one of his father Robin's eight children, including sister Arabella
![Two men in casual shirts, jumpers and jeans kneel on a grey carpeted floor looking through what is clearly an extensive archive of old papers and photos.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/680/cpsprodpb/4b1e/live/2dc74420-9e42-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Justin and Dominic Hardy worked through their late father's archive
Filming began in Shetland in the spring of 2025.
While the two leads are played by Game of Thrones and Rose of Nevada actor Francis Magee, and Norwegian actress Christiane Schaldemose, the rest of the cast was found locally.
